objectives.description: Create .claude/hooks/guard-destructive-git.sh modeled on block-pr-submission.sh (stdin JSON parse, early exit 0 on empty command, clean-tree-first exit 0, anchored destructive pattern matching, marker check with consume-on-use, exit 2 + stderr, final exit 0)
Confirm corrective stderr message names git-snapshot.sh as remedy

verification_notes: Scenario-tested in two disposable /tmp git repos (never touched this working tree): git reset --hard blocked on dirty tree (exit 2 + stderr); allowed on clean tree; git stash/git stash pop/git restore --staged all allowed on dirty tree; git checkout -- <path> and git restore <path> (no --staged) blocked; git checkout -b (no force) allowed, git checkout -f blocked; git clean -fd blocked, git clean -n allowed; git stash drop/clear blocked; benign quoted commit message containing 'reset --hard' allowed; empty/non-Bash command allowed; /todo-style safety-commit -> clean tree -> reset --hard + clean -fd both allowed; fresh marker consumed (deleted) exactly once then blocks retry; stale (>120s) marker does not authorize and is left untouched.
